GeneralSettings.Enabled.t: Blendon Switch every Blendon feature on or off at once. OFF Every feature sleeps and its keys go back to the Editor, as if Blendon were not installed. ON Each feature follows its own switch in the list below. Nothing is lost while it is off

GeneralSettings.ShowTutorial.t: Tutorial Badge A small badge in the corner of the Scene View while the tutorial is under way. Click it to open this checklist. HOW Each task ticks itself off when you actually do the gesture, in any order, and the badge flashes its name as it does. Off hides the badge and pauses the checklist. Your progress is kept

GeneralSettings.ShowShortcutTips.t: Shortcut Tips Explain a key the first time you press it. HOW When one of Blendon's keys took over an Editor command, or two commands share it, a card in the Scene View names both and where to change them. Once per key per session. Armed again whenever a binding changes

GeneralSettings.EscapeKeepsContext.t: Esc Keeps Context Pressing Esc in the Scene View never drops you out of Blendon's tools. ON Esc still cancels a grab, a typed value or a menu. The tool context stays on Game Object (Blendon). OFF Unity's own way: Esc switches to the Game Object context and Unity's Move, Rotate and Scale. Pick Game Object (Blendon) again to come back. Picking Game Object by hand still works

GeneralSettings.AnimationEnabled.t: Animate Move the camera smoothly instead of cutting straight to the new view. ON A short camera flight shows where you went. OFF The view jumps there at once. Default for every page that doesn't override it

GeneralSettings.AnimationDuration.t: Duration How long a camera transition takes, in seconds. EXAMPLES 0.2 - quick 1 - slow and easy to follow Default for every page that doesn't override it

GeneralSettings.RmbCancelEnabled.t: Right Click Cancels Right-click in the middle of a drag to call it off. HOW The selection jumps back exactly where the drag started, for handles and G / R / S grabs alike. Default for every page that doesn't override it
GeneralSettings.RmbCancelEnabled.src: Right Click Cancels Right-click in the middle of a drag to call it off. HOW The selection jumps back exactly where the drag started, for handles and {key:Blendon/Grab} / {key:Blendon/Grab Rotate} / {key:Blendon/Grab Scale} grabs alike. Default for every page that doesn't override it

GeneralSettings.RestrictDragToActiveView.t: Active View Only With several Scene Views open, draw the gizmo you drag only in the view you drag in. ON The other views stay calm while you work. OFF The dragged gizmo shows in every open Scene View at once.

GeneralSettings.CursorWrapEnabled.t: Cursor Wrap Never run out of room mid-drag. ON At the view border the cursor jumps to the opposite side, and the drag keeps going. OFF The cursor can leave the view, and the drag goes no further than the screen edge. Default for every page that doesn't override it

GeneralSettings.CursorWrap.t: Cursor Wrap Method How the cursor gets back into view at the border. OPTIONS • OS Native - Blendon moves the cursor itself. The border is set in Wrap On. • Unity - Unity's own edge jumping, at the Scene View border. • Clamp To View - no jump. The drag stops at the border. Default for every page that doesn't override it

GeneralSettings.WrapBounds.t: Wrap On The border where the cursor wraps around. OPTIONS • Scene View Viewport - the drawn 3D area • Unity Window - the whole Editor, so a drag crosses the Hierarchy and Inspector first • Screen Boundary - the display the cursor is on OS Native only. The other methods always wrap at the view's own edge

GeneralSettings.AxisColorX.t: X Axis Color Color of everything Blendon draws for the X axis: arrows, rings, boxes and lines. Starts from the look preset picked on the gizmo pages. Reset puts back that preset's color

GeneralSettings.AxisColorY.t: Y Axis Color Color of everything Blendon draws for the Y axis: arrows, rings, boxes and lines. Starts from the look preset picked on the gizmo pages. Reset puts back that preset's color

GeneralSettings.AxisColorZ.t: Z Axis Color Color of everything Blendon draws for the Z axis: arrows, rings, boxes and lines. Starts from the look preset picked on the gizmo pages. Reset puts back that preset's color

GeneralSettings.OutlineColor.t: Outline Color The thin rim that keeps Blendon's overlays readable on any background. WHERE Around the center dot, the vertex-snap markers and pie menu labels. Default for every page that doesn't override it

GeneralSettings.ToggleContextShortcut.t: Toggle Blendon Switch between Blendon's tools and the tool context you were in before, such as Game Object or ProBuilder's. KEY B HOW From any other context it goes to Game Object (Blendon). From there it goes back where you came from, or to Game Object when that context is gone or not known yet. OUTSIDE IT Unity's own feel: Grab, Vertex Snapping, Box Select and Click Selects Parent step aside and their keys do what they do in plain Unity. Navigation, the pies and the context menu stay. Works in every window, not only the Scene View
GeneralSettings.ToggleContextShortcut.src: Toggle Blendon Switch between Blendon's tools and the tool context you were in before, such as Game Object or ProBuilder's. KEY {key:Blendon/Tool Context/Toggle Blendon} HOW From any other context it goes to Game Object (Blendon). From there it goes back where you came from, or to Game Object when that context is gone or not known yet. OUTSIDE IT Unity's own feel: Grab, Vertex Snapping, Box Select and Click Selects Parent step aside and their keys do what they do in plain Unity. Navigation, the pies and the context menu stay. Works in every window, not only the Scene View

OrbitSelectedSettings.Enabled.t: Orbit Selected Turn the view around what you are working on. HOW Hold Mouse 2 and drag. The camera circles the selection, which stays in the middle of the view. Off frees both shortcuts for the Editor
OrbitSelectedSettings.Enabled.src: Orbit Selected Turn the view around what you are working on. HOW Hold {key:Blendon/Orbit Selected} and drag. The camera circles the selection, which stays in the middle of the view. Off frees both shortcuts for the Editor

OrbitSelectedSettings.ShowPivotDot.t: Show Pivot Dot See what the view is turning around. HOW With nothing selected, a dot marks the orbit point while you drag.

OrbitSelectedSettings.Depth.t: Depth With nothing selected, orbit around what is under the cursor. ON Aim at a surface and drag: the view turns around that exact point. OFF Orbits around Unity's scene pivot, like the default Scene View.

OrbitSelectedSettings.HorizontalOrbitDeg.t: Horizontal Sensitivity How fast side-to-side mouse movement turns the view. EXAMPLES 0.25 - a quarter degree per pixel, the default 1 - one degree per pixel

OrbitSelectedSettings.VerticalTiltDegree.t: Vertical Sensitivity How fast up-and-down mouse movement tilts the view. EXAMPLES 0.2 - the default 1 - one degree per pixel

OrbitSelectedSettings.AltSnapEnabled.t: Snap View To World Axis Lock onto a straight front, side or top view mid-orbit. HOW Hold Alt while orbiting: the view snaps to the nearest axis and turns orthographic. Release to orbit freely again.
OrbitSelectedSettings.AltSnapEnabled.src: Snap View To World Axis Lock onto a straight front, side or top view mid-orbit. HOW Hold {setting:OrbitSelectedSettings.SnapModifier} while orbiting: the view snaps to the nearest axis and turns orthographic. Release to orbit freely again.

OrbitSelectedSettings.SnapModifier.t: Axis Snap Key The key you hold mid-orbit to snap the view. KEY Alt by default. None switches the snap off. If the orbit shortcut has it too (Alt + Mouse 0), let go of it and press it again to snap.

OrbitSelectedSettings.SnapThresholdDegre.t: Snap Threshold How close to straight-on the view must be before it snaps. EXAMPLES 12 - within 12 degrees, the default 30 - grabs the axis from further away

OrbitSelectedSettings.RollEnabled.t: Quick Roll Flick the mouse to swing the view 90 degrees. HOW Hold Alt+Mouse 2, then flick in any direction. The view rolls that way and lands on the nearest front, side or top view.
OrbitSelectedSettings.RollEnabled.src: Quick Roll Flick the mouse to swing the view 90 degrees. HOW Hold {key:Blendon/Quick Roll}, then flick in any direction. The view rolls that way and lands on the nearest front, side or top view.

OrbitSelectedSettings.RollThresholdPixel.t: Flick Distance How far the mouse must travel before a flick counts. EXAMPLES 6 px - quick, the default 20 px - fewer accidental rolls

OrbitSelectedSettings.AnimationEnabled.t: Animate Fly to the rolled view instead of cutting to it. ON A short camera flight shows where you went. OFF The view jumps there at once. Follows Defaults on the Overview page until you tick Override

OrbitSelectedSettings.Shortcut.t: Orbit Shortcut What you hold to orbit. KEY Mouse 2 - hold, then drag. Mouse buttons only. The left one (Mouse 0) needs Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it. CANCEL Right-click or Esc mid-orbit puts the view back.
OrbitSelectedSettings.Shortcut.src: Orbit Shortcut What you hold to orbit. KEY {key:Blendon/Orbit Selected} - hold, then drag. Mouse buttons only. The left one (Mouse 0) needs Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it. CANCEL Right-click or Esc mid-orbit puts the view back.

OrbitSelectedSettings.RollShortcut.t: Quick Roll Shortcut What you press to arm a roll flick. KEY Alt+Mouse 2, then flick. Mouse buttons only. The left one (Mouse 0) needs Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it.
OrbitSelectedSettings.RollShortcut.src: Quick Roll Shortcut What you press to arm a roll flick. KEY {key:Blendon/Quick Roll}, then flick. Mouse buttons only. The left one (Mouse 0) needs Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it.

PanSettings.Enabled.t: Camera Pan Slide the view sideways without turning the camera. HOW Hold Shift+Mouse 2, then move the mouse. The scene follows the cursor. Off frees the shortcut, handing it back to the Editor
PanSettings.Enabled.src: Camera Pan Slide the view sideways without turning the camera. HOW Hold {key:Blendon/Camera Pan}, then move the mouse. The scene follows the cursor. Off frees the shortcut, handing it back to the Editor

PanSettings.InvertDrag.t: Invert Drag Reverse the pan direction. OFF Drag right and the scene follows the cursor, like pulling a sheet of paper. ON Drag right and the camera moves right, so the scene slides left.

PanSettings.Depth.t: Depth Keep the exact point you grabbed under the cursor. ON Pans at the depth of whatever is under the cursor when you start, so that point sticks to the cursor, near or far. OFF Pans at the depth of the view's pivot, so nearer things slide faster than the cursor and farther ones slower.

PanSettings.CursorWrapEnabled.t: Cursor Wrap Never run out of room mid-pan. ON At the view border the cursor jumps to the opposite side, and the pan keeps going. OFF The cursor can leave the view, and the pan goes no further than the screen edge. Follows Defaults on the Overview page until you tick Override

PanSettings.CursorWrap.t: Cursor Wrap Method How the cursor gets back into view at the border. OPTIONS • OS Native - Blendon moves the cursor itself. The border is set in Wrap On. • Unity - Unity's own edge jumping, at the Scene View border. • Clamp To View - no jump. The pan stops at the border. Follows Defaults on the Overview page until you tick Override

PanSettings.WrapBounds.t: Wrap On The border where the cursor wraps around. OPTIONS • Scene View Viewport - the drawn 3D area • Unity Window - the whole Editor, so a drag crosses the Hierarchy and Inspector first • Screen Boundary - the display the cursor is on OS Native only. The other methods always wrap at the view's own edge

PanSettings.Shortcut.t: Pan Shortcut What you hold to pan the view. KEY Shift+Mouse 2 - hold, then drag. CHANGE IT Click the field, then press a mouse button. The left one (Mouse 0) needs Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it.
PanSettings.Shortcut.src: Pan Shortcut What you hold to pan the view. KEY {key:Blendon/Camera Pan} - hold, then drag. CHANGE IT Click the field, then press a mouse button. The left one (Mouse 0) needs Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it.

ZoomSettings.Enabled.t: Zoom Blender-style scroll-wheel zoom for the Scene View. HOW Roll the mouse wheel over the Scene View to zoom in and out. Off gives the wheel back to Unity and frees the Numpad keys

ZoomSettings.ZoomTo.t: Zoom To What stays put on screen while everything grows around it. OPTIONS • Cursor - whatever is under the cursor. The default • Selection - the selected object. Several: the Pivot Point set in the toolbar • Center - the middle of the view With nothing selected in view, Selection zooms to the middle

ZoomSettings.Method.t: Zoom Method How a scroll turns into zoom, as in Blender. OPTIONS • Scale - one even step per notch, toward the pivot. The default • Dolly - flies the camera forward along its view • Continue - scroll faster to zoom further Blender: Preferences > Navigation > Zoom Method

ZoomSettings.Speed.t: Wheel Sensitivity How far one notch of the wheel zooms. EXAMPLES 0.1 - fine steps 0.5 - big jumps

ZoomSettings.InvertDirection.t: Invert Direction Swap the wheel over. OFF Scroll up to zoom in. ON Scroll up to zoom out.

ZoomSettings.KeyboardEnabled.t: Keyboard Zoom Zoom from the keypad too. KEYS Num + - zoom in Num - - zoom out TIP Each press zooms toward the point set in Zoom To, like the wheel. Off frees both keys for the Editor
ZoomSettings.KeyboardEnabled.src: Keyboard Zoom Zoom from the keypad too. KEYS {key:Blendon/Zoom/Zoom In} - zoom in {key:Blendon/Zoom/Zoom Out} - zoom out TIP Each press zooms toward the point set in Zoom To, like the wheel. Off frees both keys for the Editor

ZoomSettings.KeyboardStep.t: Keyboard Step How much one key press zooms. EXAMPLES 0.2 - a fifth of the view per press 0.5 - half of it A zoom-out press exactly undoes a zoom-in press

OrientationGizmoSettings.Enabled.t: Orientation Gizmo A Blender-style axis ball in the corner of the Scene View. HOW • Click a handle - look down that axis • Drag inside - orbit the view • Click the center - perspective or orthographic Replaces Unity's own scene gizmo

OrientationGizmoSettings.HideNativeGizmo.t: Hide Unity's Gizmo Keep only Blendon's gizmo on screen. ON Unity's scene gizmo leaves the Scene View and its Overlays menu. OFF Both gizmos show, and they can overlap.

OrientationGizmoSettings.Radius.t: Size How big the gizmo is, in pixels. EXAMPLES 45 - the default 80 - large and easy to hit

OrientationGizmoSettings.Opacity.t: Opacity How solid the gizmo is drawn. EXAMPLES 1 - solid 0.4 - see-through, the scene shows behind it

OrientationGizmoSettings.Padding.t: Padding Empty margin between the gizmo and the edge of its overlay. Too little can clip the outer handles

OrientationGizmoSettings.LineThicknessSc.t: Line Thickness How thick the axis lines and handle rims are. EXAMPLES 0.6 - the default 2 - bold

OrientationGizmoSettings.OrbitEnabled.t: Drag To Orbit Orbit without moving into the viewport. HOW Drag anywhere inside the gizmo to turn the camera. Uses the Orbit Selected sensitivity

OrientationGizmoSettings.AnimationEnable.t: Animate Fly to the clicked view instead of cutting to it. ON A short camera flight shows where you went. OFF The view jumps there at once. Follows Defaults on the Overview page until you tick Override

OrientationGizmoSettings.MiddleClickTogg.t: Middle-Click Projection Middle-click the gizmo to switch perspective and orthographic. HOW Press the middle mouse button anywhere over the gizmo.

OrientationGizmoSettings.CenterCircleEna.t: Center Circle A button in the gizmo's middle for perspective or orthographic. HOW Click the small circle in the center to switch projection.

OrientationGizmoSettings.DirectionLabelE.t: View Name Name the view when you look straight down an axis. HOW A label such as Front or Top appears under the gizmo.

OrientationGizmoSettings.NegativeLabelsA.t: Negative Letters Label the opposite handles too. OFF The -X, -Y and -Z handles show their letter only on hover. ON They are always labelled.

OrientationGizmoSettings.ShowBackground.t: Show Background A dark panel behind the gizmo, there all the time. ON The axis ball sits on a dark square and stays easy to read over a bright scene. OFF Nothing behind it, the scene shows around the handles. Unlike Hover Backdrop, it stays when the cursor leaves Also in the gizmo's right-click menu

OrientationGizmoSettings.BackdropColor.t: Hover Backdrop The circle behind the gizmo while the cursor is over it.

OrientationGizmoSettings.BackgroundColor.t: Depth Fade The color handles fade toward as they point away from you. Stands in for the scene background, which a skybox hides

ViewportNavSettings.Enabled.t: Numpad Views Blender's keypad navigation for the Scene View. KEYS • Num 1 Num 3 Num 7 - front, right, top views • Num 5 - perspective or orthographic • Num 2 Num 4 Num 6 Num 8 - orbit in steps • Num 9 - reverse view, Num 0 - camera view NumLock must be on. Off frees every key for the Editor
ViewportNavSettings.Enabled.src: Numpad Views Blender's keypad navigation for the Scene View. KEYS • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Front} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Right} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Top} - front, right, top views • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Toggle Projection} - perspective or orthographic • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Down} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Left} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Right} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Up} - orbit in steps • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Reverse View} - reverse view, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Align To Camera} - camera view NumLock must be on. Off frees every key for the Editor

ViewportNavSettings.AnimationEnabled.t: Animate Fly to the new view instead of cutting to it. ON A short camera flight shows where you went. OFF The view jumps there at once. Follows Defaults on the Overview page until you tick Override

ViewportNavSettings.OrbitStepDegrees.t: Orbit Step How far each Num 2, Num 4, Num 6 or Num 8 press turns the view. EXAMPLES 15 - the default, 6 presses make a right angle 45 - 2 presses make a right angle
ViewportNavSettings.OrbitStepDegrees.src: Orbit Step How far each {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Down}, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Left}, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Right} or {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Up} press turns the view. EXAMPLES 15 - the default, 6 presses make a right angle 45 - 2 presses make a right angle

ViewportNavSettings.MatchFieldOfView.t: Match Field of View Frame exactly what the camera sees. ON Align To Camera copies the camera's field of view too. OFF Only position and rotation. The Scene View keeps its own wider or narrower view.

SharedGizmoSettings.GhostColor.t: Ghost Color Tint of the Drag Ghost, the see-through marker left where a drag started. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.PrecisionModeEnabled.t: Precision Mode Slow a drag right down for fine adjustments. HOW Hold Shift while dragging any handle. The selection moves at a fraction of the cursor's speed, and the Ctrl snap step halves. The key and the speed are set in the two rows below. Shared by every gizmo
SharedGizmoSettings.PrecisionModeEnabled.src: Precision Mode Slow a drag right down for fine adjustments. HOW Hold {setting:SharedGizmoSettings.PrecisionModifier} while dragging any handle. The selection moves at a fraction of the cursor's speed, and the Ctrl snap step halves. The key and the speed are set in the two rows below. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.PrecisionModifier.t: Precision Key The key you hold mid-drag for Precision Mode. WHILE HELD • the drag slows to Drag Speed % • the Ctrl snap step halves None switches Precision Mode off. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.PrecisionFactor.t: Precision Drag Speed How far the selection travels for the same cursor movement while the precision key is held. EXAMPLES 0.2 - a fifth as far as the cursor 0.5 - half as far Lower is finer. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.AimModifier.t: Aim at Surface Hold a key mid-drag to aim at the surface under the cursor. WHAT IT DOES • Move - drops the selection onto that surface: a floor, a wall, another object • Rotate - turns the selection to face that point KEY Alt by default. None switches it off. Move and Rotate follow this key until their own page overrides it

SharedGizmoSettings.AxisExcludeModifier.t: Plane Lock Limit a drag to a plane instead of a single axis. DURING A DRAG OR A GRAB X, Y or Z - only along that axis Shift+Z - along X and Y, never along Z This row picks the key held with the letter, Shift by default. Shared by every gizmo
SharedGizmoSettings.AxisExcludeModifier.src: Plane Lock Limit a drag to a plane instead of a single axis. DURING A DRAG OR A GRAB X, Y or Z - only along that axis {setting:SharedGizmoSettings.AxisExcludeModifier}+Z - along X and Y, never along Z This row picks the key held with the letter, Shift by default. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.AxisLabelsEnabled.t: Axis Labels Name the axis you are dragging. HOW While an axis handle is dragged, its letter - X, Y or Z - appears near its tip, so the axis is named, not only colored. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.Quality.t: Resolution How smooth the gizmo's rings and curves look. HOW Every curve is drawn from straight segments. Higher uses more of them: smoother, and a little slower to draw. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.Size.t: Scale Size of every Blendon gizmo on screen. EXAMPLES 1 - default size 2 - twice as big Each tool's own page multiplies this value. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.ShowPreview.t: Show Preview A live picture of the gizmo above each tool's Appearance settings. WHY See what every slider does without looking at the Scene View. It slowly spins to show every angle. Shows the gizmo at rest. Hover and drag states appear only in the Scene View

SharedGizmoSettings.Opacity.t: Opacity How solid the gizmos are drawn. EXAMPLES 1 - fully solid 0.5 - see-through, the object shows underneath Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.PivotMenuEnabled.t: Pivot Point Menu Blender's pivot point for Blendon's tools: what a multi-object selection turns and scales around. WHERE Blendon's Pivot Point dropdown in the Tool Settings overlay. It takes the place of Unity's Pivot / Center while one of Blendon's tools is active. MODES • Bounding Box Center - middle of the box around the selection • Median Point - average of the objects' origins • Individual Origins - each object around its own origin • Active Object - around the last object clicked Off leaves the dropdown just Center and Pivot

SharedGizmoSettings.PerObjectLocalAxes.t: Per-object Local Axes In Local space, every selected object follows its own axes, as in Blender. OFF - UNITY All objects move along the active object's axes. ON - BLENDER Each object moves, turns and scales along its own axes, still around the shared pivot point. Individual Origins always uses each object's own axes. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.Contrast.t: Color Contrast How vivid the gizmo's axis colors are. EXAMPLES 1 - exactly as set in Axis Colors below 2 - brighter, further from gray 0.5 - muted Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.ThresholdDegrees.t: Fade Out Angle Hide handles you see edge-on. WHY An arrow pointing straight at you, or a plane seen side-on, is too thin to grab. Within this many degrees of that angle it fades out. 0 never fades. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.DragGhostsEnabled.t: Drag Ghost Mark where a drag started. HOW While you drag, a see-through copy of the handle stays at the start point, so you can see how far you have moved. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.CursorWrapEnabled.t: Cursor Wrap Never run out of room mid-drag. ON At the view border the cursor jumps to the opposite side, and the drag keeps going. OFF The cursor can leave the view, and the drag goes no further than the screen edge. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.CursorWrap.t: Cursor Wrap Method How the cursor gets back into view at the border. OPTIONS • OS Native - Blendon moves the cursor itself. The border is set in Wrap On. • Unity - Unity's own edge jumping, at the Scene View border. • Clamp To View - no jump. The drag stops at the border. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.WrapBounds.t: Wrap On The border where the cursor wraps around. OPTIONS • Scene View Viewport - the drawn 3D area • Unity Window - the whole Editor, so a drag crosses the Hierarchy and Inspector first • Screen Boundary - the display the cursor is on OS Native only. The other methods always wrap at the view's own edge

SharedGizmoSettings.ClickSelectEnabled.t: Click-select Click through a gizmo to select the object behind it. HOW A click on a handle, with no drag, selects whatever is under the cursor. Dragging the handle works as usual. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.CenterDotRadius.t: Center Dot Size Size of the dot that marks the gizmo's pivot point. TIP It grows and turns white while the Aim at Surface key is held. The smallest value hides it. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.CenterDotOutlineThic.t: Center Dot Outline Width of the dark rim around the center dot, in pixels. Its color is Outline, under Axis Colors below. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.CenterDotColor.t: Center Dot Color Fill color of the dot that marks the gizmo's pivot point. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.TooltipInfoEnabled.t: Live Readout The exact change, shown while you drag. SHOWS Distance, angle or scale factor in a box in the Scene View, for example dz: 1.40 m Global. TIP Type a number mid-drag for an exact value. It shows here as you type. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.TooltipInfoSnapToCur.t: Snap to Cursor Keep the live readout right next to the cursor. OFF Fixed near the top of the Scene View. Move it with Top Offset below. ON Follows the cursor, so your eyes stay on the drag. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.TooltipInfoTopOffset.t: Readout Position How far down the Scene View the Live Readout sits. EXAMPLES 0 - top edge 0.5 - middle 1 - bottom edge Not used while Snap to Cursor is on. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.ScreenRingThickness.t: Screen Ring Thickness Line width of the white circle in the gizmo's center, in pixels. THE RING • Move - drag it to move freely, parallel to the view • Scale - drag it to scale evenly on every axis Also sets the width of the rotation sweep lines and snap ticks. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.ConstraintLineThickn.t: Constraint Line The line that shows where a locked drag can go. WHEN While a drag is locked to an axis or plane, a line runs through the pivot along the whole path the selection can take. This sets its width, in pixels. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.ConstraintLineOpacit.t: Constraint Line Opacity How solid the Constraint Line is drawn. EXAMPLES 1 - solid 0.3 - faint, the scene shows through Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.ConstraintLineContra.t: Constraint Line Contrast How vivid the Constraint Line's axis color is. EXAMPLES 1 - as set in Axis Colors 2 - brighter, further from gray Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.SnapTicksEnabled.t: Snap Ticks See every snap step before you let go. HOW Hold Ctrl while dragging to snap, as usual in Unity. A tick marks each snap step along the dragged axis, plane or ring. Step sizes come from Unity's Grid and Snap settings. The precision key doubles the ticks. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.SnapTickLength.t: Snap Tick Length How long each Snap Tick is. A fraction of the handle's size. Shared by every gizmo

SharedGizmoSettings.SnapTickGap.t: Snap Tick Gap Empty space between the handle and its Snap Ticks. A fraction of the handle's size. 0 starts the ticks right at the handle. Shared by every gizmo

MoveGizmoSettings.SurfaceSnapEnabled.t: Surface Snap Drop the selection onto whatever is under the cursor. HOW Hold Alt while dragging a move handle. The selection lands on the floor, wall or object beneath the cursor. A drag locked to an axis or plane keeps its lock, and snaps only as far as it can reach
MoveGizmoSettings.SurfaceSnapEnabled.src: Surface Snap Drop the selection onto whatever is under the cursor. HOW Hold {setting:MoveGizmoSettings.SurfaceSnapModifier} while dragging a move handle. IsolateViewSettings.Enabled.t: Isolate View Hide everything except the selection. HOW Press Num / to isolate what you selected. Press it again to bring the scene back. Hides with Unity's Scene Visibility, so nothing in the scene is changed
IsolateViewSettings.Enabled.src: Isolate View Hide everything except the selection. HOW Press {key:Blendon/Isolate View} to isolate what you selected. Press it again to bring the scene back. Hides with Unity's Scene Visibility, so nothing in the scene is changed

IsolateViewSettings.IncludeChildren.t: Include Children Keep each selected object's children visible too. ON The whole hierarchy under the selection stays. OFF Only the objects you selected stay; their children hide.

IsolateViewSettings.FrameOnIsolate.t: Frame On Isolate Frame the selection the moment you isolate it. OFF The camera stays where it is. ON The camera flies to the selection, the same as Frame Selected.

IsolateViewSettings.Shortcut.t: Isolate Shortcut What you press to isolate the selection, and again to restore the scene. KEY Num /
IsolateViewSettings.Shortcut.src: Isolate Shortcut What you press to isolate the selection, and again to restore the scene. KEY {key:Blendon/Isolate View}

BoxSelectSettings.Enabled.t: Box Select Drag a box in the Scene View to select everything it touches, the way Blender does. WHILE DRAGGING Shift+Mouse 0 - add to the selection Ctrl+Mouse 0 - remove from it Shift + Ctrl - see Shift + Ctrl Clicking still selects the Editor's way. Off hands the box back to the Editor
BoxSelectSettings.Enabled.src: Box Select Drag a box in the Scene View to select everything it touches, the way Blender does. WHILE DRAGGING {key:Scene View/Add Box Select} - add to the selection {key:Scene View/Invert Box Select} - remove from it Shift + Ctrl - see Shift + Ctrl Clicking still selects the Editor's way. Off hands the box back to the Editor

BoxSelectSettings.SelectPrefabRoots.t: Select Prefab Roots Touch any part of a prefab and the whole prefab is selected. ON The prefab instance itself, as the Editor's own box does. OFF Only the parts the box touched.

BoxSelectSettings.RequireFullyEnclosed.t: Fully Enclosed Select only objects that fit entirely inside the box. OFF - BLENDER Anything the box touches, even a sliver of it. ON - UNITY Only whole objects inside the box.

BoxSelectSettings.CombinedMode.t: Shift + Ctrl What a box does with Shift and Ctrl held together. OPTIONS • Difference - flips everything under the box: selected objects drop out, the rest are added • Intersect - keeps only what was selected and is also under the box Follows the Editor's Add and Invert Box Select shortcuts if you rebind them

BoxSelectSettings.RespectSelectionBase.t: Respect Selection Base Touch part of an object and select its parent marked [SelectionBase], the way a click does. WHICH ONE The nearest marked parent wins. Inside a prefab, a marked object below the root wins over the root. Off ignores [SelectionBase], like the Editor's own box

BoxSelectSettings.VisibleOnly.t: Visible Only Select only what you can see inside the box, like Blender with X-Ray off. ON Objects hidden behind others are left alone. OFF The box reaches through walls and selects hidden objects too. Press C to switch it, even mid-drag. Sprites, lines and trails are always tested whole
BoxSelectSettings.VisibleOnly.src: Visible Only Select only what you can see inside the box, like Blender with X-Ray off. ON Objects hidden behind others are left alone. OFF The box reaches through walls and selects hidden objects too. Press {key:Blendon/Box Select Visible Only} to switch it, even mid-drag. Sprites, lines and trails are always tested whole

BoxSelectSettings.ClickSelectsParent.t: Click Selects Parent Click the selected object again to climb to its parent. EACH CLICK 1 selects the object 2 its parent 3 the next parent up ... past the top, the object under the cursor again Reaches every level, even parts under a prefab root. Clicks with Shift or Ctrl are left alone. Works in the Game Object (Blendon) context only

BoxSelectSettings.SelectionUpdate.t: While Dragging What you see before you let go of the mouse button. OPTIONS • On Release - nothing, until the button comes up • Highlight - marks what will be selected • Live - selects for real as you drag, Hierarchy and Inspector included Highlight stays fast in big scenes. Live can make the drag stutter

BoxSelectSettings.CursorInfo.t: Cursor Readout A label at the box's corner that tells you what letting go will change. OPTIONS • Count - the total, plus how many are added (+) and removed (-) • Names - the objects that change • Count And Names - both • None - no label

BoxSelectSettings.HierarchyKeys.t: Hierarchy Keys Walk the hierarchy from the Scene View, as in Blender. KEYS [ - up to the parents ] - down to the children Shift+[ or Shift+] - add them, keep what is selected Objects with nowhere to go stay selected. Off frees the keys
BoxSelectSettings.HierarchyKeys.src: Hierarchy Keys Walk the hierarchy from the Scene View, as in Blender. KEYS {key:Blendon/Select Parent} - up to the parents {key:Blendon/Select Children} - down to the children {key:Blendon/Add Parent To Selection} or {key:Blendon/Add Children To Selection} - add them, keep what is selected Objects with nowhere to go stay selected. Off frees the keys

BoxSelectSettings.OutlineStyle.t: Outline Style How the box's border is drawn. OPTIONS • Solid - a plain line • Dashed - marching ants • Dashed Dense - the same, twice as dense

BoxSelectSettings.OutlineColor.t: Outline Color Color of the box's border.

BoxSelectSettings.FillColor.t: Fill Color Tint inside the box while you drag. Keep the alpha low, so the scene shows through

BoxSelectSettings.HighlightStyle.t: Highlight Style How Highlight marks the objects the box will select. OPTIONS • Fill - a see-through overlay on the whole object • Outline - a line around its silhouette • Both - the two together Lights, cameras and empties get a square at their position instead

BoxSelectSettings.HighlightOutlineWidth.t: Outline Width Thickness of the line around each marked object, in screen points. EXAMPLES 0.5 - a hairline 3 - bold Used by the Outline and Both styles

BoxSelectSettings.HighlightOccludedOpaci.t: Occluded Opacity How strongly the hidden parts of a marked object show, the parts behind other geometry. EXAMPLES 1 - as strong as the visible parts 0.5 - fainter 0 - not shown

BoxSelectSettings.HighlightColor.t: Highlight Color Color of the objects the box will add. ALPHA Sets how strong the fill is. An outline is always solid. With Shift held, objects already selected are not marked

BoxSelectSettings.DeselectHighlightColor.t: Deselect Color Color of the selected objects the box will remove: with Ctrl held, or on Difference. ALPHA Sets how strong the fill is. An outline is always solid.

BoxSelectSettings.NamesTextColor.t: Readout Text Color Color of the count and names in the Cursor Readout.

BoxSelectSettings.NamesBackgroundColor.t: Readout Background Color of the panel behind the Cursor Readout. ALPHA Sets how much of the scene shows through.

BoxSelectSettings.VisibleOnlyShortcut.t: Visible Only Shortcut What you press to switch Visible Only on and off, even in the middle of a drag. KEY C. Blender's own X-Ray key is Alt+Z.
BoxSelectSettings.VisibleOnlyShortcut.src: Visible Only Shortcut What you press to switch Visible Only on and off, even in the middle of a drag. KEY {key:Blendon/Box Select Visible Only}. Blender's own X-Ray key is Alt+Z.

BoxSelectSettings.MoveBoxShortcut.t: Move Box Hold a key mid-drag to move the whole box instead of resizing it. HOW While dragging, hold Space and move the mouse. Let go to carry on resizing from the new spot. Only listened for during a drag, so the key keeps its usual job otherwise
BoxSelectSettings.MoveBoxShortcut.src: Move Box Hold a key mid-drag to move the whole box instead of resizing it. HOW While dragging, hold {key:Blendon/Box Select Move Box} and move the mouse. Let go to carry on resizing from the new spot. Only listened for during a drag, so the key keeps its usual job otherwise

HistorySettings.Enabled.t: Selection History Step back and forward through what you selected, like a browser. BUTTONS Mouse 3 - back Mouse 4 - forward, the side buttons of most mice Keeps up to 100 steps. Off frees both buttons for the Editor
HistorySettings.Enabled.src: Selection History Step back and forward through what you selected, like a browser. BUTTONS {key:Blendon/History/Undo Selection} - back {key:Blendon/History/Redo Selection} - forward, the side buttons of most mice Keeps up to 100 steps. Off frees both buttons for the Editor

HistorySettings.BackShortcut.t: Back Jump to the previous selection. KEY Mouse 3, the rear side button by default.
HistorySettings.BackShortcut.src: Back Jump to the previous selection. KEY {key:Blendon/History/Undo Selection}, the rear side button by default.

HistorySettings.ForwardShortcut.t: Forward Jump forward again after going back. KEY Mouse 4, the front side button by default.
HistorySettings.ForwardShortcut.src: Forward Jump forward again after going back. KEY {key:Blendon/History/Redo Selection}, the front side button by default.

ViewHistorySettings.Enabled.t: View History Step back and forward through camera views, like a browser. BUTTONS Shift+Mouse 3 - back Shift+Mouse 4 - forward Keeps up to 100 steps. Off frees both buttons for the Editor
ViewHistorySettings.Enabled.src: View History Step back and forward through camera views, like a browser. BUTTONS {key:Blendon/History/Undo View} - back {key:Blendon/History/Redo View} - forward Keeps up to 100 steps. Off frees both buttons for the Editor

ViewHistorySettings.AnimationEnabled.t: Animate Fly to the recalled view instead of cutting to it. ON A short camera flight shows where you went. OFF The view jumps there at once. Follows Defaults on the Overview page until you tick Override

ViewHistorySettings.AnimationDuration.t: Duration How long the camera flight takes, in seconds. EXAMPLES 0.2 - quick 1 - slow and easy to follow Follows Defaults on the Overview page until you tick Override

ViewHistorySettings.BackShortcut.t: Back Return to the previous camera view. KEY Shift+Mouse 3
ViewHistorySettings.BackShortcut.src: Back Return to the previous camera view. KEY {key:Blendon/History/Undo View}

ViewHistorySettings.ForwardShortcut.t: Forward Go forward again after going back. KEY Shift+Mouse 4
ViewHistorySettings.ForwardShortcut.src: Forward Go forward again after going back. KEY {key:Blendon/History/Redo View}

PieMenuSettings.Enabled.t: Pie Menus Blender's radial menus: hold a key, flick toward an item, let go. TWO WAYS Flick hold the key, move toward an item, release Tap press and release quickly: the menu stays open for a click Off frees every menu's key, built-in and custom. The menus are listed at the bottom of this page

PieMenuSettings.Radius.t: Radius How far the items sit from the menu's center, in pixels. EXAMPLES 60 - compact 100 - default 200 - spread wide

PieMenuSettings.Threshold.t: Deadzone How far the cursor must move from the center before it points at an item. EXAMPLES 12 - a small nudge is enough 40 - forgiving, for a shaky hand Let go inside it and the menu closes without running anything

PieMenuSettings.ConfirmThreshold.t: Confirm Distance Run the item once the cursor is this far past the deadzone and stops, with the key still held. EXAMPLES 0 - off: only releasing the key runs an item 60 - flick far, pause, and it runs

PieMenuSettings.TapTimeout.t: Tap Timeout The longest press that still counts as a tap, in seconds. HOW Release the key faster than this without moving: the menu stays open and you click an item. Hold it longer and it works as a flick. 0.2 s is Blender's own value

PieMenuSettings.AnimationTimeout.t: Unfold Time How long the items take to spring out from the center, in seconds. EXAMPLES 0 - in place at once 0.06 - a quick pop 0.3 - slow, easy to follow

PieMenuSettings.RecenterTimeout.t: Recenter Timeout Keep aiming from where you pressed, after a menu is nudged away from a view edge. HOW A menu opened near an edge moves inward to fit. For this long, directions are still measured from the point where the cursor really was. 0 turns it off, as Blender ships it

PieMenuSettings.LockCursorToViewport.t: Lock Cursor To Viewport Keep the cursor inside the Scene View while a pie menu is open. OFF The cursor can wander onto another window or monitor, and the gesture is lost.

PieMenuSettings.PlaceOnFloor.t: Place On Floor Objects created from a pie rest on the point you clicked, instead of sinking halfway in. HOW The new object is lifted by half its height. Applies to Add Object items in any pie

PieMenuSettings.ShowAccelerators.t: Show Numbers Number each item. Press its digit to run it, no aiming needed. The top-row digits always work. The keypad needs NumLock on

PieMenuSettings.ItemColor.t: Item Color Background of an item that is neither pointed at nor current.

PieMenuSettings.HighlightColor.t: Highlight Color Background of the item the cursor points at.

PieMenuSettings.CurrentColor.t: Current Color Background of the item that matches the Editor right now: the active tool, the draw mode, a snap that is on.

PieMenuSettings.TextColor.t: Text Color Item labels and the menu's title.

PieMenuSettings.RingColor.t: Center Ring Color The ring at the menu's center, which shows the way you are pointing.

WireframeToggleSettings.Enabled.t: Toggle Wireframe Blender's Shift+Z: Wireframe and back with one key. HOW Press once for Wireframe. Press again to return to the draw mode you came from. Has its own switch, so it keeps working with the pie menus off

WireframeToggleSettings.Shortcut.t: Toggle Wireframe Shortcut What you press to go to Wireframe and back. KEY Shift+Z Returns to Shaded when there is no earlier mode
WireframeToggleSettings.Shortcut.src: Toggle Wireframe Shortcut What you press to go to Wireframe and back. KEY {key:Blendon/Toggle Wireframe} Returns to Shaded when there is no earlier mode

SceneMenuSettings.Enabled.t: Context Menu Right-click the Scene View for Blendon's menu: the Editor's entries, grouped and searchable. INSIDE • every entry of the Editor's own menu • Cut, Copy, Paste and the rest as a row of icons • a search field: type, then Enter Shift + right-click opens the Editor's own menu. Off hands the right-click back

SceneMenuSettings.EditActions.t: Edit Actions How Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Rename and Delete are shown. OPTIONS • Icon Row - one row of icon buttons at the top, like Windows 11 • List - ordinary rows with names and keys

SceneMenuSettings.SearchField.t: Search Field A search box in the menu's header. HOW Just start typing: every entry is filtered, submenus included. Enter runs the best match. Off leaves the header to the selection's name

SceneMenuSettings.ClassicMenuRow.t: Classic Menu Row A row at the bottom that opens the Editor's own context menu. Shift + right-click opens that menu either way

SceneMenuSettings.AddObject.t: Add Object An Add submenu: empty, primitives, light, camera, particles. WHERE IT LANDS Where you right-clicked: on the surface under the cursor, or on the grid. Placed the same way as the Add Object pie

SceneMenuSettings.RepeatLast.t: Repeat Last Run the last entry again. The row names it, for example Repeat Snap to Floor. Works for Blendon's entries and the Editor's

SceneMenuSettings.FrameSelected.t: Frame Selected Frame the selection from the menu. HOW Runs Blendon's Frame Selected cycle when that page is on, the Editor's framing otherwise.

SceneMenuSettings.SnapToFloor.t: Snap to Floor Drop the selection onto the surface below it. SAME AS Blendon's Snap to Floor key, End.
SceneMenuSettings.SnapToFloor.src: Snap to Floor Drop the selection onto the surface below it. SAME AS Blendon's Snap to Floor key, {key:Blendon/Snap To Floor}.

SceneMenuSettings.ResetTransform.t: Reset Transform A Reset submenu: position, rotation, scale, or all three. Saves a trip to the Inspector. Parts already at rest are greyed out

SceneMenuSettings.AlignToActive.t: Align to Active Move the rest of the selection onto the active object. OPTIONS Position, Rotation, or both. The active object is the one you selected last

SceneMenuSettings.TransformClipboard.t: Transform Clipboard Copy one object's transform onto others. STEPS 1 Copy Transform on the source 2 select the targets 3 Paste Transform Position, rotation and scale together

SceneMenuSettings.TransformClipboardInli.t: Inline Put Copy Transform and Paste Transform side by side on one row. OFF One under another, a row each.

SceneMenuSettings.HideAndShow.t: Hide & Show Hide, Hide Others and Show All, right in the menu. HOW Uses Unity's Scene Visibility, the eye column in the Hierarchy. Hides in the Scene View only. Nothing in the scene changes

SceneMenuSettings.HideAndShowInline.t: Inline Put Hide, Hide Others and Show All side by side on one row. OFF One under another, a row each.

SceneMenuSettings.SelectRelated.t: Select Related Children, Hierarchy and Parent side by side on one row, to walk the hierarchy. OPTIONS • Children - the direct children • Hierarchy - the whole subtree • Parent - one level up With Inline off they move into a Select submenu

SceneMenuSettings.SelectRelatedInline.t: Inline Put Children, Hierarchy and Parent side by side on one row. OFF They move into a Select submenu.

SceneMenuSettings.Grouping.t: Group & Unparent Tidy the hierarchy from the Scene View. ENTRIES • Group - puts the selection under a new empty parent • Unparent - moves it out to the top of the scene

SceneMenuSettings.GroupingInline.t: Inline Put Group and Unparent side by side on one row. OFF One under another, a row each.

SceneMenuSettings.ExtraOrderText.t: Which order Blendon's own entries come out in inside the menu section they belong to

SceneMenuSettings.Shortcut.t: Context Menu Shortcut The button that opens the menu. KEY Mouse 1 - a click. Holding it to fly through the scene still works. Listed as Blendon/Context Menu in Unity's Shortcuts window
SceneMenuSettings.Shortcut.src: Context Menu Shortcut The button that opens the menu. KEY {key:Blendon/Context Menu} - a click. Holding it to fly through the scene still works. Listed as Blendon/Context Menu in Unity's Shortcuts window

SharedGizmoSettings.AllToolsEnabled.t: All Tools Turns Blendon's four transform gizmos on or off in one click. TOOLS • Move W • Rotate E • Scale R • Transform Y On only while all four are on. A tool switched off falls back to Unity's own gizmo
SharedGizmoSettings.AllToolsEnabled.src: All Tools Turns Blendon's four transform gizmos on or off in one click. TOOLS • Move {key:Tools/Move} • Rotate {key:Tools/Rotate} • Scale {key:Tools/Scale} • Transform {key:Tools/Transform} On only while all four are on. A tool switched off falls back to Unity's own gizmo

TransformMoveSettings.AxisHeadFlat.t: Flat Tips Draw the arrow tips as flat triangles that always face you. OFF Solid 3D cones, shaded like objects in the scene. ON Flat shapes that read the same from every angle.

TransformRotateSettings.RingDepthGradien.t: Depth Gradient Show which way a ring tilts. HOW While a ring is dragged, its near half is drawn bright and its far half dark, so it reads in 3D. Off draws the ring in one flat color

TransformRotateSettings.AngleArcEnabled.t: Angle Arc See how far you have turned. HOW While you drag a ring, the wedge between the start angle and the current one is filled in.

TransformRotateSettings.AngleArcOpacity.t: Angle Arc Opacity How solid the Angle Arc fill is. EXAMPLES 0.35 - default 1 - solid

TransformRotateSettings.DynamicOpacity.t: Dynamic Opacity Keep the angle arc readable past a full turn. HOW Every 360-degree lap stacks another layer of fill. On, the fill thins out, so the stack stays at the opacity above instead of turning white.

TransformScaleSettings.AxisHeadFlat.t: Flat Boxes Draw the boxes as flat squares that always face you. OFF Solid 3D cubes, shaded like objects in the scene. ON Flat squares that read the same from every angle.

Blendon/Tool Context/Toggle Blendon.t: Toggle Blendon Switch between Blendon's tools and the tool context you were in before, such as Game Object or ProBuilder's. KEY B HOW From any other context it goes to Game Object (Blendon). From there it goes back where you came from, or to Game Object when that context is gone or not known yet. OUTSIDE IT Unity's own feel: Grab, Vertex Snapping, Box Select and Click Selects Parent step aside and their keys do what they do in plain Unity. Navigation, the pies and the context menu stay. Works in every window, not only the Scene View Click to open this shortcut on the Keyboard page

Blendon/Vertex Snap.t: Vertex Snapping Place an object exactly on another object's vertex. HOW 1 Hold V - the gizmo jumps to the vertex nearest the cursor. 2 Drag onto another object - that vertex lands on its nearest vertex. 3 Release the mouse to drop. Replaces Unity's own vertex snapping, in the Game Object (Blendon) context only. The Unity keyboard preset on the Overview page gives Unity's back its key Click to open this shortcut on the Keyboard page

HOW 1 Hold {key:Blendon/Vertex Snap} - the gizmo jumps to the vertex nearest the cursor. 2 Drag onto another object - that vertex lands on its nearest vertex. 3 Release the mouse to drop. Blendon/Pick Virtual Pivot.t: Pick Virtual Pivot Use any vertex as a temporary pivot to turn and scale around. HOW 1 Press Shift+V - the vertex under the cursor is ringed. 2 Click to settle on it - the gizmo jumps there. 3 Drag any handle - the selection turns and scales around that point. Pan.t: Camera Pan Slide the view sideways without turning the camera. HOW Hold Shift+Mouse 2, then move the mouse. The scene follows the cursor. Off frees the shortcut, handing it back to the Editor Click to open the Pan page
Pan.src: Camera Pan Slide the view sideways without turning the camera. HOW Hold {key:Blendon/Camera Pan}, then move the mouse. The scene follows the cursor. Off frees the shortcut, handing it back to the Editor Click to open the Pan page

Zoom.t: Zoom Blender-style scroll-wheel zoom for the Scene View. HOW Roll the mouse wheel over the Scene View to zoom in and out. Off gives the wheel back to Unity and frees the Numpad keys Click to open the Zoom page

Numpad Views.t: Numpad Views Blender's keypad navigation for the Scene View. KEYS • Num 1 Num 3 Num 7 - front, right, top views • Num 5 - perspective or orthographic • Num 2 Num 4 Num 6 Num 8 - orbit in steps • Num 9 - reverse view, Num 0 - camera view NumLock must be on. Off frees every key for the Editor Click to open the Numpad Views page
Numpad Views.src: Numpad Views Blender's keypad navigation for the Scene View. KEYS • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Front} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Right} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/View Top} - front, right, top views • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Toggle Projection} - perspective or orthographic • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Down} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Left} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Right} {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Orbit Up} - orbit in steps • {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Reverse View} - reverse view, {key:Blendon/Viewport Nav/Align To Camera} - camera view NumLock must be on. Off frees every key for the Editor Click to open the Numpad Views page

Orientation Gizmo.t: Orientation Gizmo A Blender-style axis ball in the corner of the Scene View. HOW • Click a handle - look down that axis • Drag inside - orbit the view • Click the center - perspective or orthographic Replaces Unity's own scene gizmo Click to open the Orientation Gizmo page

All Tools.t: All Tools Turns Blendon's four transform gizmos on or off in one click. TOOLS • Move W • Rotate E • Scale R • Transform Y On only while all four are on. A tool switched off falls back to Unity's own gizmo Click to open the All Tools page
All Tools.src: All Tools Turns Blendon's four transform gizmos on or off in one click. TOOLS • Move {key:Tools/Move} • Rotate {key:Tools/Rotate} • Scale {key:Tools/Scale} • Transform {key:Tools/Transform} On only while all four are on. A tool switched off falls back to Unity's own gizmo Click to open the All Tools page

Move.t: Move Tool Blendon's Blender-style gizmo for Unity's Move tool W. HANDLES • Arrows - move along one axis • Squares - move across a plane • Ring - move freely, parallel to the screen Off gives the tool back to Unity's own gizmo and frees the Grab key Click to open the Move page
Move.src: Move Tool Blendon's Blender-style gizmo for Unity's Move tool {key:Tools/Move}. Frame Selected.t: Frame Selected Bring the selection into view. Press again to cycle closer. EACH PRESS 1 Selection Center - turn to the middle of the selection 2 Active Pivot - turn to the active object's pivot 3 Zoom In - close in with Unity's own frame 4 Back to Start - the view you started from The Sequence table changes the steps and their order. Off frees the key for the Editor Click to open the Frame Selected page

Isolate View.t: Isolate View Hide everything except the selection. HOW Press Num / to isolate what you selected. Press it again to bring the scene back. Hides with Unity's Scene Visibility, so nothing in the scene is changed Click to open the Isolate View page
Isolate View.src: Isolate View Hide everything except the selection. HOW Press {key:Blendon/Isolate View} to isolate what you selected. Press it again to bring the scene back. Hides with Unity's Scene Visibility, so nothing in the scene is changed Click to open the Isolate View page

Snap to Floor.t: Snap To Floor Drop the selection onto the surface below it. HOW Press End: each object falls straight down and rests on whatever it hits. NOTHING BELOW It rests on the Terrain under it, or on the ground plane at Y = 0 without one. An object buried in terrain comes back up onto it. Ignores the object's own colliders. Fully undoable Click to open the Snap to Floor page
